findings.exact_text: The build creates an onedir distribution, copies licenses/help/specs, archives it and computes SHA-256. Windows CI also compiles installer/PatchTrace.iss with Inno Setup into PatchTrace-Windows-x64-Setup.exe, writes a SHA-256 sidecar, installs it under a path containing spaces and Unicode, runs the installed frozen self-test, and silently uninstalls it. The installer compiler is build-only and is not needed on user systems. Beta binaries are unsigned. Keep Qt DLLs replaceable in the onedir distribution. Update by unpacking a new version separately; projects are never overwritten by updater. Back up projects before future schema migration.

findings.exact_text: The Windows CI packaging change adds an Inno Setup per-user wrapper around the already-tested dist/PatchTrace one-folder bundle. The installer requires Windows x64, targets the current user's LocalAppData, adds a Start Menu shortcut, and has no setup-time downloads, administrator requirement, custom actions or runtime prerequisites. The compiler is a CI build dependency, not a user dependency. The installer is unsigned, consistent with SPEC-52. CI verifies install, Qt DLL/plugin presence, the packaged --self-test, and uninstall from a temporary path containing spaces and Unicode. This row records the implemented acceptance gate; pass status is pending the final Windows workflow run on the release branch.
